task.title: Complete POC acceptance coverage and documentation
task.description:
Close the remaining gaps between what Workbook does and what its tests and README claim, so the POC can be published as a beta.

The original scope read: cover history replay, cache reconstruction, SHA variants, renderer parity, HTTP routes, installer behavior, and final README alignment. A 2026-08-06 audit at commit c453596 established what each of those already has. `go test ./...` passes with no failures. Coverage by package: autosync 100.0, presentation 98.5, terminalui 91.9, agentdocs 87.2, webui 84.9, cli 84.6, core 83.2, gitstore 78.4, syncloop 78.5, perf 76.3, projection 74.8, historyvalidation 73.9, userconfig 72.9. The audit found no test that asserts nothing: no err-is-nil-only tests, no table tests whose rows all take the same branch. Many tests carry comments naming the production mutation they kill. Three of the seven original items are effectively done and are struck from scope below.

Already covered, no further work:
- History replay. Divergent-history replay across two clones and a bare remote (internal/gitstore/sync_test.go:52, 755, 787, 850), all three conflict types (internal/gitstore/reconcile_test.go:14, 61 and sync_test.go:109), parked-ref lifecycle (reconcile_test.go:127-286), CLI level (internal/cli/autosync_test.go:148-237, internal/cli/sync_test.go:76-159), projection replay (internal/projection/operations_test.go:15-79), checkpoint replay including interruption and resume (internal/historyvalidation/validator_test.go).
- Cache reconstruction. Deletion, malformed, wrong-project, missing-table, failed-replacement, cross-process replacement, and head-change-during-build are all covered (internal/projection/store_test.go:1023-1215, operations_test.go:52, internal/cli/run_test.go:488), plus the validation cache equivalents (internal/historyvalidation/cache_test.go:400-521).
- HTTP routes at handler level. Every registered route in internal/webui/handler.go:223-239 has at least one handler test, including 404 and 405 shapes and hostile-content escaping.
- Installer behavior. scripts/install_test.go and scripts/setup_dev_env_test.go execute the real scripts; the release chain is covered by internal/release/release_test.go and the three scripts/*_release_test.go files.

## Remaining work

1. Same-field concurrency witness. No test has two clones set the same field to different values. The only same-field status test uses the same value on both sides (internal/gitstore/reconcile_test.go:101-122). README:929 claims every other concurrent field change is last-syncer-wins, with no test pinning it. Add a gitstore test where two clones set one task status to different values, asserting last-syncer-wins convergence and no conflict entry. Closes the AGENTS.md expectations for concurrent edits to the same field and for conflicting status changes.

2. SHA-256 end to end. Only the gitstore read and classify layers plus the perf harness run against SHA-256 repositories. Every fetch, push, sync, and reconcile integration test, and all of internal/cli, internal/projection, internal/historyvalidation, and the webui serve tests, run SHA-1 only, because internal/testrepo does a plain git init with no --object-format. Add an object-format option to internal/testrepo, then (a) one gitstore Fetch/Push/Sync/replay/conflict test against a SHA-256 repo and SHA-256 bare origin, and (b) one CLI lifecycle covering create, update, delete, restore, rebuild, and validate in a SHA-256 repo. Skip-guard them the way internal/gitstore/read_test.go:1010 does.

3. Serve-level route wiring. DELETE /api/tasks/{id}, POST /api/tasks/{id}/restore, and GET /api/tasks/{id}/history have no test through the real runServe wiring; they are covered only handler-level with injected fakes. This is not hypothetical: backlog task WB-01KZBM37EZJXV0ZBC53SJ4NVVC records that swapping the delete and restore function literals in runServe compiles and leaves the whole suite green while board deletion is broken. Existing serve-level tests cover status, position, dependencies, create, update, list refresh, and /api/sync (internal/cli/run_test.go:1130-1537, internal/cli/watcher_test.go:513). Coordinate with WB-01KZBM37EZJXV0ZBC53SJ4NVVC rather than duplicating it; the options-struct refactor and these tests are two halves of the same fix.

4. README alignment. Concrete mismatches found:
   - The route list at README.md:642-658 omits GET /api/sync and PUT /api/sync, registered at internal/webui/handler.go:237-238. Verified: the string api/sync appears zero times in README. Commit 2fae0b7 added the routes, the toggle UI, and tests without touching README.
   - The web board section does not mention the publication-mode indicator and toggle, or the optimistic per-task mutation queue from commits 0d1546b and eaaee47. The queue is documented only at docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-06-optimistic-web-mutation-queue-design.md, which itself needs correcting per the queue bug ticket.
   - The implemented-command block prints create, list, update, delete, and restore bare, although all five accept --json plus --no-sync and field flags (internal/cli/flags.go:223-307). This contradicts the blocks own preamble that commands marked --json support the machine-readable envelope. move, depend, free, and next omit --no-sync.
   - README.md:16 and :1052 still say conflict reconciliation remains proposed, while the reconciling-divergent-histories section from :532 describes it as implemented, which it is, with tests.
   - There is no consolidated exit-code table anywhere. Exit 8 appears inline at :74 and :563, exit 4 at :353, and exit 6 is never documented despite being produced by ref compare-and-swap, push local-changed, validation head drift, and requireExpectedHead. For an agent-facing tool the table is load-bearing. Note that next deliberately exits 0 while reporting conflicts (internal/cli/run.go:731-737), which the blanket statement at :74 does not carve out.
   - Update TestREADMEImplementedCommands in the same change: it pins the stale text against a second hardcoded copy of the same strings (internal/cli/run_test.go:906-935) rather than deriving from commandSchemas, so it currently enforces the omission instead of catching it. Deriving expectations from commandSchemas would end the triple maintenance across the schema, the test map at run_test.go:1039-1045, and the README.

5. Bootstrap variants. Fresh-clone bootstrap is covered (internal/cli/sync_test.go:296, internal/gitstore/sync_test.go:262). Shallow and single-branch clones have zero coverage: --depth and --single-branch appear nowhere in test code, though AGENTS.md:73 names both. Add setup plus fetch/sync tests for each.

6. Renderer parity, cheap version. Parity today is by construction: both renderers consume internal/presentation, which sits at 98.5 percent coverage, and each side is tested alone. No test feeds one task set to both renderers and compares presented facts. Add one cross-check asserting identical prefixes, priorities, titles, labels, and dependency summaries. Note the two boards genuinely diverge on unknown statuses, the terminal showing an UNKNOWN STATUS section and the web hiding them; that divergence is being removed under a separate ticket, so sequence this after it or assert the corrected behavior.

7. Installer edges. Two untested README claims: the default destination $HOME/.local/bin being created when needed (every existing test passes an explicit destination), and the PATH export hint printed when the destination is off PATH (scripts/install.sh:61).

8. Multi-process concurrency. AGENTS.md:75 expects multiple worktrees and multiple processes. Worktrees are covered (internal/gitstore/config_test.go:514, 566, internal/historyvalidation/cache_test.go:467, 521). Multiple OS processes are not: every concurrency test uses goroutines in one process, and TestStoreWritesToTheCacheAnotherProcessReplaced only simulates the second process. Add one test spawning two built workbook binaries mutating the same repository concurrently; the scripts package already builds binaries and can be reused. Stretch goal, but this is the scenario a multi-agent beta creates.

Items 1 through 4 are load-bearing for the beta. Items 5 through 8 are completeness.

Not in scope, correctly: remote claims and commit linkage are marked proposed in README and have no tests, which is consistent; multi-parent tips are rejected by design, so merged-history coverage means the rejection test at internal/gitstore/read_test.go:616.

CI is a prerequisite for this task meaning anything. The suite currently reports ok while skipping 36 web client tests when node is absent, and there is no push or pull-request workflow at all. That is tracked separately; land it first or this coverage can silently stop running.
